Body.Content:
Multiple factors, such as seasonal adjustments, promotions, and market dynamics, influence a product’s active sales price and cause it to fluctuate over time. Businesses need a reliable way to detect and act on these changes:

Retail stores must update shelf labels promptly to reflect the latest prices.

E-commerce websites must notify shoppers about price drops for items in their shopping carts to help drive conversion.

Price change tracking in Unified pricing management lets organizations automatically identify items whose prices have changed since the last tracking run. Instead of comparing the full catalog each time, the system captures only the delta - that is, the items with price changes within a given time window.

Key benefits include:

Automated change detection: Eliminates the need for stakeholders to manually identify items that have undergone price changes.

Delta-based tracking: Surfaces only items with price differences since the last tracking run, reducing noise and focusing attention on relevant changes.

Improved performance: By limiting reports to changed items, price report generation is significantly faster compared to full-catalog reports.

Output:

Price change tracking data entity: All detected price changes are recorded in the price change tracking data entity, making them available for external reporting and downstream integrations.

Delta price report generation: Price managers can generate reports in Unified pricing management that include only items with price changes since the last report generation, which streamlines the review process.

GA date: December CY2026

Preview date: October CY2026
